text.p: Rural services group IAMA Ltd on Thursday gave an undertaking to the Queensland Supreme Court that it would not despatch a formal Part A takeover document to fellow rural group Primac Holdings Ltd, a Primac spokesman said.
A further court hearing has been set down for next Monday.

The IAMA undertaking follows legal action taken by Primac on Wednesday to prevent despatch of a revised IAMA Part A takeover offer. IAMA is offering nine of its shares for every 10 Primac, an offer Primac directors have said appeared inadequate.

Talks with IAMA to achieve adequate disclosure in the Part A documents had broken down, Primac chairman Steve Morrow said on Wednesday. Primac subsequently made application to the court to restrain despatch of IAMA's revised Part A, Morrow said.

Morrow declined to comment on reports that Primac was having talks of its own with rival rural groups Wesfarmers Ltd and Elders Australia Ltd. Primac is scheduled to hold its annual meeting on Friday in Brisbane.
